acceptance.requirement: Every member has distinct discoveryFacts, classificationFacts, and dispatchInvestigation layers; the legacy all-nodes-full-investigation schema and fallback are rejected.
Dispatch-grade paths are non-placeholder, repository-relative, existing when required, and issue-specific.
Not-applicable values use stable machine reason codes, never empty strings, TODO, N/A, or empty-array padding.
Discovered and dependency-classified members can remain shallow without code, test, or current-doc paths.
Classification alone cannot produce an implementation prompt; complete current dispatch investigation is mandatory.
Projection inputs and per-member evidence derive from one versioned selector receipt; root cannot construct or silently rewrite scope.
Unchanged per-member inputs are reused idempotently and unrelated member drift does not invalidate unaffected layers.
Issue or relevant-comment drift invalidates only the affected member discovery/classification and downstream dispatch layers.
Base SHA or delivery-epoch drift invalidates dispatchInvestigation without discarding valid discovery/classification.
AGENTS, current-doc, owner-code, and test-entry identity drift invalidates the affected dispatchInvestigation.
Investigation priority is deterministic and auditable: ready-adjacent, unlocking, critical-path, high-priority, then long-wait.
Machine-ready stage work and free slots are dispatched before background investigation; root cannot suppress ready nodes.
Long-running deep investigation records blockedSince, blocker owner, evidence, and a stable starvation denial.
Root scheduler only verifies selector/proposal receipts and manages resources; it cannot author semantic or dispatch investigation facts.
The Sol/max read-only one-shot DAG agent owns only discovery/classification semantic proposals.
The Sol/max test owner owns dispatch-grade investigation and may write only the issue test contract paths.
Discovery agents and prose cannot author ready or a legal phase transition.
The Sol/low implementer consumes a frozen prompt and returns test-contract-disputed for any owner/design/acceptance gap.
Every implementation prompt is issue-specific, base-bound, receipt-bound, and includes acceptance, counterexamples, commands, probes, mutations, failure classes, and stop conditions.
A 100-node selected scope can dispatch two ready-adjacent test owners without deep-investigating the other 98 nodes.
With at least fifteen eligible stage candidates, fifteen slots stay filled and background investigation cannot starve dispatch.
Shared indexes may be reused, but every acceptance-group member keeps issue-specific paths, constraints, owner, acceptance map, and investigation digest.
The executable DAG gate calls validateInvestigationProjection on the current selector-bound projection; importing the symbol without invoking it is insufficient.

Corrected #1816 uses a validated layered projection. Production scripts contain no dot- or bracket-syntax legacy investigation fallback, compile rejects legacy node authority, and direct eligibility without a validated layered projection is never dispatchable.
A discovery-complete node with no classification is a valid reachable discovered phase and is neither test-owner nor implementation dispatchable.
Discovery/classification facts reject root authorship and require the exact DAG creator/updater Sol/max read-only proposal authority.
Layer digests are recomputed from content and every required dispatch evidence path must exist; arbitrary 64-hex values are not authority.
The valid implementation task carries all seven revision-1 bindings: test owner, epoch, classification digest, AGENTS chain, allowed test paths, acceptance group, and member evidence digest.
Dispatch investigation transition rejects a test-owner candidate with any wrong model or effort.
Owner-code and test-entry digest drift invalidate only dispatchInvestigation and must never report reuse=true.
A deeply investigated member appears exactly once in scheduler output as implementation work and is removed from the dispatch-investigation queue.
